Before we proceed, I want to outline how this case conference will work. I'll hear from each participant in turn. Each person will have the opportunity to formally place relevant facts or prior arrangements on the case record. I'll confirm that everyone has had a chance to speak, and then I'll make a decision on the appropriate resolution path and any working arrangements during that process.

As you may know, our organization handles workplace conduct concerns through either a formal investigation or a mutually agreed restorative process. I'll be determining which path is appropriate based on what we discuss today.

Let's begin. Could each of you introduce yourselves and share your perspective on what's been happening? I'd like to start with whoever feels ready to go first.

Thank you, Maya. I'll share my perspective now.

Regarding the prior agreement Daniel just placed on the record — I want to be clear about my response. I did have a private conversation with Daniel, and the two terms he described — three facilitated repair sessions and routing work requests through the shared project channel — are accurate as far as they go. However, that agreement was reached informally, and it was never added to the case file, as Daniel himself acknowledged. I'm glad it's on the record now.

Now, regarding my condition: I need unscheduled direct one-to-one contact with Daniel to be prohibited during any restorative process. I want to explain why. The agreement to use the shared project channel instead of direct messages was part of how we were trying to manage our working relationship. But the issue that gave rise to this complaint is broader than just our messaging habits — it's about how our disagreements have been handled in group discussions. I've found that when Daniel and I interact one-on-one without a facilitator or a structured setting, it tends to escalate tensions that then spill over into our group discussions. Prohibiting unscheduled one-to-one contact during the restorative process would create a safer, more structured environment for both of us to actually repair the working relationship.

I'm not refusing to cooperate — quite the opposite. I'm willing to participate fully in a restorative process with a neutral facilitator, as Rosa described. I just need that boundary in place so the process can succeed.

That's my perspective and my response to what's been placed on the record so far.

Thank you, Maya. I appreciate the opportunity to share my full perspective.

First, regarding the prior agreement — I'm glad Leah has confirmed the terms are accurate. I want to acknowledge that the agreement was informal and never added to the case file, and I take responsibility for that gap. That's exactly why I felt it was important to place it on the record today.

Regarding Leah's condition about prohibiting unscheduled direct one-to-one contact — I want to respond thoughtfully. I understand her concern that unstructured one-on-one interactions can escalate tensions that spill over into group discussions. I don't have an objection in principle to limiting unscheduled direct contact during the restorative process. In fact, the agreement we already reached — to route work requests through the shared project channel rather than direct messages — was a step in that same direction. I'd be comfortable with Maya incorporating that boundary into the working arrangements, as long as it doesn't prevent us from completing necessary project work through the appropriate channels.

As for what's been happening in group discussions — I want to be honest about my role in this. I recognize that some of my disagreements with Leah in group settings have been handled in ways that weren't productive and that contributed to the complaint. I don't think either of us set out to create a difficult dynamic, but I can see how our back-and-forth in those settings became a pattern that others found disruptive. I'm genuinely committed to the three facilitated repair sessions we agreed to, and I believe a restorative process with a neutral facilitator, as Rosa outlined, is the right path forward.

I'm willing to participate fully and in good faith. I think the prior agreement we reached, combined with Leah's boundary and the procedural requirements Rosa placed on the record, give us a solid foundation for that process. That's my perspective.
